header_notes: Rig 10 PASSED: the live Base set of Oct 22 is byte-identical to what was tested (live 350 of 350 checks PASS, dry-run 349 of 349, 0 mismatches, 0 incomplete). So every finding tagged LIVE and CONFIRMED below is present in the deployed contracts (HH-008 is app code, not a contract).

Ceremony dry-run gas: every one of the 72 transactions was sent at the 16,777,216 gas cap (Base per-transaction maximum, EIP-7825). Actual use was 30,295 to 4,247,636 per transaction (109,844,802 total), so none came near the cap.
Fix-phase note: rigs/hardhat also adds an npm script 'ceremony:dryrun' to base-contracts/package.json. That is outside testing-rigs/ and was not brought to main.
class_rule: CONFIRMED VULNERABILITY = reproduced by a PoC; SPEC CONFLICT = code differs from Rev 6/12/13 with no exploit shown; UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION = static or reasoning only; INCOMPLETE TESTING = a tool could not finish, which is not evidence of safety. Rigs that already classify their findings keep their class; assumption-gap findings are classified by this rule.
scope_rule: LIVE (Base set) = reachable on the live Base set today (Base-only app config, commit 5a21665; only Base ETH has a usable scheduled price). LIVE (ERC-20 path) = in a live Base contract but only reachable once an ERC-20 is priced or locked. LIVE (on-chain; gated only by non-Base prices not yet posted) = the non-Base reader is registered in the live finalized Base Verifier (rig 9 read-only check); the app's Base-only config hides the UI but does not block direct contract calls, so one posted price for that asset opens the path. LATENT (non-Base only) = non-Base path not yet rechecked against the rig 9 correction. N/A = tooling coverage, not a code path.

findings.description: Assumed: The header is part of the source chain's settled (finalized) history, on the named chain Gap: Only keccak(header) == claimed hash, claimed height == header number, and claimed chain id == the reader's own constant. The claimed chain id is the caller's word; an Ethereum header carries no chain id. Nothing ties the header to any real chain. EthereumLockReader (beacon light client) exists but the ceremony registers SimpleEthereumLockReader; the checkers/ finality contracts are never called by any reader. Exploit: Run a local fork, create a real-looking lock, then rewrite header fields (mixHash, parentHash) so the header exists on no chain; the receipt proof still matches its receiptsRoot. Submit with claimed chain id 1. Known Oct 22 finding (non_base_finality_trust_model.test.cjs): about 311 VCLM per forged lock.
findings.damage_potential: Unlimited VCLM mint up to the 500,000,000 hard cap, and CHONX after activation, with no real asset locked. Inflated supply also inflates RAC and stake rewards.
evidence: ADVERSARIAL=1 FINDING ADV-01 minted 310.96 VCLM. Cross-ref AG-01.
ADVERSARIAL=1 FINDING ADV-02 minted 310.96 VCLM. AG-01.

spec: Rev 6 VF-XCH-006/008: no issuance before documented exact finality; relayer cannot waive finality. Code accepts a self-consistent header with no finality at all. Mitigation in config only: commit 5a21665 says the live Base ceremony is Base-only until settled-history checkers exist; build_ceremony_artifacts.cjs still ships these readers.
Rev 6 (every mint traces to a real lock)
findings.note: EVM readers (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche) confirmed by ADV-01..06, ADV-10. Mint and RAC both need a usable scheduled price for the lock's asset row: recordFeeAndRac (VinculumFinalisVerifier.sol:646, USD at :682) and verifyAndMint (:796) both call _resolveVerifiedGrossUsd, which reverts 'VF-ORC-005: no usable scheduled price' (:997) unless a price is already bound, and a binding (:1009) is only written by an earlier call that itself had a price. So RAC does NOT bypass the price gate (ADV-07/08/09 recorded RAC only because the rig's fixture posted those prices). Today only Base ETH is priced and, per rig 9's read, no non-Base row aliases it, so the gate is one applyScheduledPriceRun by the single price poster (see AG-07) away from opening. Static reading for the price-gate claim; the forgeries themselves are PoC-reproduced.

findings.description: Assumed: One RAC per real fee payment; racIdentity is derived from the lock's immutable facts Gap: The only check is !recordedRacs[racIdentity]. racIdentity is free caller input, so the same proven lock can record RAC any number of times, before or after it mints. Exploit: Create one real Base lock (about $2.39 in the PoC). Call recordFeeAndRac K times with K random racIdentity values. epochRewardBasis grows K times; allocateEpoch mints basis*10 VCLM to stakers. PoC: 50 records paid 358.8 VCLM of stake rewards versus 7.176 honest.
findings.damage_potential: Stake reward VCLM inflated without bound (until the VCLM cap), diluting every holder; attacker who stakes captures it. Works today on the Base-only ceremony.

findings.description: Assumed: Prices come from the twice-daily scheduled run; a record is valid until the next run; the poster has no value authority Gap: Only poster identity, runId > last, price > 0. No bound, no timestamp, no staleness. runId = 2^64-1 freezes all later runs forever (prices can never update or be marked failed). Exploit: A compromised or mistaken poster posts 1000x price and mints from a tiny lock; or posts runId 2^64-1 to freeze prices. PoC: a 0.001 ETH lock minted 31,096 VCLM.

findings.description: Assumed: Token balances held by the lock do not change on their own Gap: Inbound fee-on-transfer is handled (balance delta). Rebasing is not: one shared pool, fixed principal per lock. Negative rebase makes the last releasers insolvent; positive rebase is stuck. Fee to Dev Fund uses transfer(fee) with no received check. No on-chain rebasing reject in the registry. Exploit: If any rebasing token is registered on a non-Base chain, a negative rebase shifts the loss to whoever releases last.

findings.description: Assumed: The fee went to the configured Dev Fund for that environment Gap: The Dev Fund check is commented out ('In simulation: skip'). devFundDestinations is written by configureDevFund but never read at mint; the reader/lock Dev Fund is never compared with it. Exploit: Register (or point at) a lock whose devFund is the attacker; fee goes back to the attacker, mint still succeeds. PoC AG-09: verifier Dev Fund set to one address, lock fee to another, mint succeeds with junk devFundDestination and zero evidence.
findings.damage_potential: Fees can bypass the Dev Fund while still earning issuance and RAC; makes the fee cost of an attack zero when combined with a misconfigured or forged source.

findings.description: The USDC/USDT $0.95 rule is applied at the first Verifier submission, not at lock creation, in both directions. The spec says a stablecoin below $0.95 is unavailable for every new lock, and that an existing lock keeps its creation price. (a) Depeg after the lock: a USDT lock created at $1.00 and first submitted after a run at $0.94 is refused with VF-ORC-005; the fee is kept and no VCLM is issued while the price stays below $0.95. (b) Lock during a depeg: the lock contracts have no $0.95 check, so a USDC_X lock is accepted at $0.94 and the fee taken. The Verifier refuses it while the price is below $0.95, but the refusal leaves the lock unbound, so after a later run at $1.00 it mints at $1.00. This happens even when the record was attempted at creation. Only the app is meant to refuse the lock; a direct contract call skips that.
findings.damage_potential: (b) Buy a depegged USDC/USDT row, lock it, and mint at the recovered price: about 6% more VCLM per dollar at a $0.94 depeg, scaling with depeg depth. (a) Fee paid with no mint during a depeg.
evidence: Part (a): 156 cells DEVIATION:valid_lock_not_minted (stable_above_then_below, VF-ORC-005), Base and Ethereum. Part (b): 308 cells DEVIATION:minted_but_spec_refuses (stable_below_then_above, 154 of them bound, with record_err_A VF-ORC-005 and the record at B succeeding), plus 4 Handshake cells where the lock was accepted, the fee taken and the later band check refused it (DEVIATION:lock_accepted_fee_taken_no_mint). Example: USDC_X lock at $0.94 worth $0.01 minted 0.138 VCLM at the $1.00 run.
findings.related: AG-06 (price bound at first submission); AG-11 (which rows the $0.95 rule catches)

findings.description: A lock that is valid at creation (in band at the creation price, fee already paid to the Dev Fund) becomes unmintable if a price run moves its USD out of band before the first submission. The Verifier re-checks the band at the later price: a Handshake that rises above $0.02 is refused with VF-COM-003, and a standard lock that falls below $0.01 is refused with VF-COM-009. The fee is kept and no VCLM is issued. The spec says a lock keeps its creation price. Root cause is AG-06 (price bound at first submission); AG-16 is the lock-side band gate.
findings.damage_potential: User pays the fee and gets no VCLM for a valid lock. Limited to locks near the band edges and to the fee amount. Principal release at maturity was not tested by this rig.
evidence: 68 cells DEVIATION:valid_lock_not_minted outside the stablecoin classes: TKN price 2 to 1 drops $0.01 and $0.015 standard locks below $0.01 (60 cells, VF-COM-009); ETH price x2 pushes $0.015 and $0.02 Handshakes above $0.02 (4 cells, VF-COM-003); TKN Handshake cases (4 cells, VF-COM-003). All on Base and Ethereum alike. Fee equals the 5% floor and reached the Dev Fund in every one.
findings.related: AG-06 (price bound at first submission is the root cause); AG-16 (lock-side band gate)

Exploit: During a depeg, a lock of an unmatched stablecoin row is valued at the depegged run without the floor rule (the floor exists to block that).

findings.description: Assumed: USD value used for the lock band gate is real Gap: The lock trusts the caller's USD for its band gate. findings.description: Assumed: Each row's decimals and token address are the real token's Gap: Rows are written by the deployer before finalize from the off-chain build; nothing checks them on chain. evidence: Static only (no PoC): build_gaps.py found no check matching: on-chain identity check (decimals/code) or signed registry hash.

findings.scope: LIVE (on-chain; gated only by non-Base prices not yet posted)
findings.description: Assumed: The reader registered for 'Ethereum' reads Ethereum Gap: Any non-zero address is accepted for any name. With AG-01, an EVM reader also accepts a testnet lock at the same CREATE address (same deployer key and nonce) because the chain id is only claimed. Exploit: Deploy the lock on a testnet with the mainnet deployer nonce, lock test ETH, mint as mainnet.
findings.damage_potential: Mint from worthless testnet assets (same root cause as AG-01).
evidence: Static only (no PoC): build_gaps.py found no check matching: reader ENVIRONMENT_ID equals the name.
findings.note: Relabeled from LATENT, split view. Recorder's own read-only check of the live Base Verifier at block 52984350 (2026-10-23 08:20 EDT, testing-rigs/live_read/live_verifier_read_2026-10-23.json): finalized, deployer zero, 15 readers registered, every non-Base native row has no usable price (Arbitrum, Optimism and Polygon rows are aliased, also unpriced). Misregistration half: not present live. Each registered reader reports an environment id equal to the name it is registered under, the six EVM readers report mainnet chain ids (1, 42161, 10, 137, 56, 43114), and registration is closed by finalize. Testnet-replay half: rides on AG-01 (the chain id is only claimed in the package), so it is live on-chain gated by a posted price, like AG-01.

findings.description: Mint after release.

findings.description: lockId is chosen by the caller and must be unused; a front-runner can use it first.
findings.damage_potential: Griefing: a watcher can take a pending lockId first so the victim's lock call reverts. No funds lost.

findings.description: The CVL measures the received amount by balance delta (good for fee-on-transfer tokens) but stores a fixed amount. A negative rebase later makes the stored amount larger than the balance. Rated low because the asset list is allowlisted.
findings.damage_potential: A token that rebases down after deposit leaves the CVL short at release.
findings.related: AG-08 (rebasing / balance-delta assumptions in the vault; HH-005 reproduces this on an Ethereum fork)

findings.description: External calls inside loops. Targets are protocol contracts, so the risk is liveness only.

findings.description: Assumed: (Rev 12) no Handshake allowance limit; no identity counter Gap: The Verifier still requires the package to state 3 (EVM/Base) or 1 (UTXO/Stellar/XRPL) from the Rev 6 allowance rule. It counts nothing, so no limit applies, but the Rev 6 field is still a required input.
findings.damage_potential: none (vestige; a wrong value only makes a mint revert)

spec: Rev 12 removes the allowance; Verifier still enforces the Rev 6 constant.

findings.description: Closed-path rule cannot hold literally; user paths classified open by design.
findings.damage_potential: The addendum asks that after finalize every non-view function reverts or is the poster path. On live, user paths stay open by design (lock, release, verifyAndMint, recordFeeAndRac, Stake and Synth user calls, token transfers). recordFeeAndRac is the HH-001 path, so an open user path is where the critical bug lives. The user/config split in WRITE_CLASS is the rig's judgement, not a spec table.
spec: Rev 6 (no spec list of post-finalize open functions)
findings.related: AG-04 / HH-001 (recordFeeAndRac is an open user path after finalize)

findings.description: CHC found a real overflow trace in forge() for a huge count. Solidity 0.8 checked math turns it into a revert, so no wrap and no free mint.
CHC overflow trace for gross * STANDARD_FEE_BPS when gross > 2^256/500. Checked math reverts. No real token has that supply. Same trace on the extracted copy (FeeMath.sol:37).

CHC underflow trace for _balanceOf(after) - beforeBal when the pulled token lowers the vault balance during transferFrom (a hostile or rebasing token). Checked math reverts, so the lock is refused. Ties to finding L04 (rebasing tokens).
CHC overflow trace for createdAt + duration. duration is limited to the fixed CommitmentDurations table, so only a solver-chosen huge timestamp reaches it. Checked math reverts.
